items.title: Jackie McLean — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: and Tadd’s music [Tadd Dameron], that whole period.

ctx.x: What do you think? Is that a function – well, it’s a function of how you developed. But, in developing musicians, where do you place the emphasis?

I’m fortunate that I have people on my staff that can cover all the bases. So if they come with me, they come to – what I call, to develop a concept. That’s what I give them. I help develop their concept by letting them experience what I experienced, what I heard, what I listened to, and what made me begin to develop. I bring it to them. Same recordings, same stuff. All the recordings that I first listened to, from the first one, which was Just You, Just Me, with Lester Young, Johnny Guarnieri, Sid Catlett, and…
Let’s go back to the beginning. Oh, there’s one other thing. There’s a jazz festival in Hartford this weekend. Have you played that festival before?
